newsitem.title: EGYPT: Somalia Salvation Council to hold talks in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Somalia Salvation Council to hold talks in Egypt.

text.p: A council of Somalia faction leaders arrived in Cairo on Friday for talks on efforts for reconciliation in their embattled country.
Airport sources reported the arrival of the National Salvation Council (NSC) delegation and said they were due to meet north Mogadishu faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed.

The NSC was formed in January in Ethiopia by 26 Somali faction leaders. Faction leader Hussein Aideed, a 34-year-old former U.S. Marine who succeeded his father Mohamed Farah Aideed on his death last August, boycotted the meeting and condemned those who attended it.
Aideed was elected Somali president by his supporters, but he and his government are rejected by most other factions.
The NSC has appealed to Aideed to desist from all acts of violence and join the peace effort for Somalia.
Somalia has been without central authority since 1991 when factions led by Mohamed Farah Aideed and his rival Ali Mahdi Mohamed ousted dictator Mohammed Siad Barre.
The leaders said when they set up their NSC that it was authorised to establish a provisional central government.
